jobs.occupation: Metabolic Engineer (m/f/d) (Molekularbiologe/-biologin)
jobs.description:
Job Title: Metabolic Engineer (m/f/d) 

Microbial CO2 Transformation Specialist 

10 September 2026 

☀️About Us: 

Join the COLIPIan family as a Metabolic Engineer and help us develop next-generation microbial CO₂ transformation processes. 

At COLIPI, we are developing sustainable bioprocesses that use renewable carbon, including CO₂, to produce valuable microbial lipids and biomaterials. Our technology combines unconventional CO₂-utilizing microorganisms, metabolic engineering, and advanced fermentation to create sustainable alternatives to conventional lipid production. 

We are looking for an experienced scientist who can combine experimental strain engineering with metabolic modelling, systems biology, enzyme engineering, and bioinformatics to improve our production strains systematically. 

🧑🏽‍🔬Key Responsibilities: 

- Identify, design, and optimize metabolic pathways for converting CO₂ into lipids and other microbial storage molecules. 
- Develop and implement strain-engineering strategies, including gene knock-outs, overexpression, heterologous pathway expression, promoter engineering, plasmid-based engineering, and CRISPR/Cas-based approaches. 
- Establish, curate, and apply genome-scale metabolic models of our unconventional production strains to identify metabolic bottlenecks, predict engineering targets, and guide strain development. 
- Select and optimize heterologous enzymes and apply enzyme-engineering approaches to improve enzyme activity, stability, expression, and performance within the host microorganism. 
- Analyze and interpret transcriptomics, metabolomics, genomic, and sequencing data to understand cellular physiology and identify new engineering opportunities. 
- Apply bioinformatics tools for genome annotation, pathway analysis, sequence comparison, enzyme identification, and promoter/regulatory-element prediction. 
- Develop genetic tools and engineering strategies for COLIPI's unconventional CO₂-utilizing microbial strains. 
- Plan, execute, and analyze metabolic and genetic engineering experiments and translate results into iterative strain-development strategies. 
- Work closely with fermentation and analytical teams to evaluate engineered strains under relevant cultivation and gas-fermentation conditions. 

🛠️Qualifications: 

- PhD in Metabolic Engineering, Synthetic Biology, Systems Biology, Biotechnology, Biochemistry, Microbiology, or a related field, ideally combined with relevant academic and/or industry experience. 
- Strong background in microbial metabolic engineering, molecular biology, genetic engineering, and synthetic biology. 
- Hands-on experience with strain-engineering techniques such as knock-out/overexpression, cloning, heterologous gene expression, CRISPR/Cas, and directed evolution. 
- Demonstrated experience with genome-scale metabolic modelling and constraint-based metabolic analysis, ideally including model reconstruction or curation and experience with metabolic-modelling tools such as COBRApy, COBRA Toolbox, CellNetAnalyzer, etc.  
- Experience analyzing omics datasets, particularly transcriptomics and metabolomics, using computational and bioinformatics tools. 
- Good programming and data-analysis skills, ideally in Python and/or R. 
- Knowledge of enzyme engineering, protein structure-function relationships, and optimization of heterologous enzymes for activity and stability in thermophilic host microbe. 
- Strong understanding of microbial physiology, central carbon metabolism, carbon fixation pathways, metabolic regulation, and cellular redox/cofactor metabolism. 
- Familiarity with fermentation processes; experience with gas fermentation, autotrophic organisms, C1 metabolism, or non-model microorganisms is a strong advantage. 
- Experience with lipid/fatty-acid metabolism or engineering of acetyl-CoA and malonyl-CoA pathways is advantageous. 
- Ability to work independently, develop scientific strategies, and contribute to building and leading a highly effective strain-engineering team. 
- Legal permit to work in Europe, fluent in English (German B2 advantageous). 
- Willingness to embrace startup dynamics and help establish scalable scientific processes for future growth. 

🥰We Offer: 

- Competitive salary and 28 days of paid holidays 
- Steep learning and growth curve 
- Laptop and personal safety gear (goggles, coat, shoes) and training  
- Be part of an international team, blending academia with passionate startup vibes 
- Work on groundbreaking climate action technology with Europe's leading microbial carbon capture experts 
- Embrace an open feedback culture, flat hierarchies, and short decision-making processes 
- Access a fully equipped lab, cutting-edge technology, and ample room for personal development 
- Participation in advanced training programs 
- Annual performance appraisal meeting with manager, in addition to more frequent feedback and growth meetings 

⛵️Location: Hamburg, Germany 

- Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere of the 2nd biggest city and 1st ranked city to live in Germany. 
- Experience unique maritime charm and blazing nightlife. 
- Immerse yourself in a city rich in cultural events, museums, and galleries. 

If you are passionate about leveraging biology to tackle climate challenges and want to be part of a dynamic team shaping the future, apply now to contribute to our mission at COLIPI.

Job Description

Are you passionate about driving inventory accuracy, optimizing processes, and creating transparency in a dynamic logistics environment? - Inventory Accuracy & Stock Control: Ensure daily alignment between physical inventory and SAP records while driving initiatives to improve stock accuracy, minimize losses, and establish sustainable inventory control standards.

Qualifications

- Professional Experience: You have proven experience in inventory management, ideally within a 3PL and multi-client logistics environment, and a strong understanding of inventory control and reconciliation processes.
- SAP & Analytical Skills: You possess extensive SAP knowledge in inventory management, reporting, and reconciliation and are highly skilled in analyzing inventory variances and deriving effective solutions.
- Process Improvement Mindset: You enjoy challenging existing processes, driving continuous improvement initiatives, and implementing sustainable solutions that enhance operational performance.
- IT & System Competence: You have advanced Excel skills and experience collaborating with SAP IT teams to optimize system processes and inventory booking procedures. A valid license for operating industrial trucks is considered an advantage.
- Language & Communication Skills: You have very good English Skills (Germans Skills are a strong Plus) and communicate confidently with clients, management, and operational teams. A proactive, responsible, solution-oriented, and collaborative mindset completes your profile.

Additional Information

- ArvatoCare – Company Health Insurance: Your health matters to us. Benefit from a complimentary supplementary health insurance plan including an annual health budget and no health check requirement.
- Responsibility from Day One: Take ownership of a critical operational function and actively shape inventory excellence within a growing logistics environment.
- Development Opportunities: Expand your professional and personal capabilities through challenging projects, continuous learning, and close collaboration with experienced colleagues and leaders.
- Corporate Benefits: Access attractive discounts and special offers across numerous well-known brands and services.

jobs.description:
Work Your Magic with us!

Ready to explore, break barriers, and discover more? We know you’ve got big plans – so do we! Our colleagues across the globe love innovating with science and technology to enrich people’s lives with our solutions in Healthcare, Life Science, and Electronics. United As One for Patients, our purpose in Healthcare is to help create, improve and prolong lives. We develop medicines, intelligent devices and innovative technologies in therapeutic areas such as Oncology, Neurology and Fertility. Our teams work together across 6 continents with passion and relentless curiosity in order to help patients at every stage of life. Joining our Healthcare team is becoming part of a diverse, inclusive and flexible working culture, presenting great opportunities for personal development and career advancement across the globe.

Your Role:

At the intersection of science, strategy, and commercial impact, this role places you at the heart of some of the most consequential decisions in healthcare drug development and commercialization. As an Associate Director within the Global Strategic Insights function, you will serve as a trusted thought partner to therapy area commercial teams — translating complex market dynamics into clear, actionable intelligence that shapes how healthcare assets are launched, grown, and managed across major global markets.

This role will interact primarily with the Rare Tumor and Specialty Therapy Area teams, partnering closely with colleagues who are driving some of the most strategically significant assets in the portfolio.

You will own the end-to-end delivery of insights across one or more GSI disciplines (primary market research, competitive intelligence, or strategic forecasting), ensuring every recommendation is grounded in rigorous analysis and directly informs critical business decisions.

Working with cross-functional partners across commercial strategy, market access and pricing, other GSI functions, and regional insights teams, you will drive insights that elevate decision quality at critical stages of the asset lifecycle.

Who You Are :

- A degree in life sciences, business, economics, or a related field — or equivalent professional experience — is required.
- 5 or more years of experience in at least one global strategic insights discipline — primary market research, competitive intelligence, data analytics, or strategic forecasting — ideally within the pharmaceutical or biopharma industry.
- You have designed and led insights and KPI workstreams for in-market or launch assets, with at least 2 years of direct experience across pre-launch, launch, and post-launch phases.
- You hold deep expertise in one or more of the following: qualitative and quantitative primary market research (study design, discussion guide development, strategic recommendations); global competitive intelligence (trial monitoring, congress coverage, strategic simulation); or topline forecasting (model building, opportunity assessment, scenario analysis).
- You have global experience across two or more major markets — such as the US, China, EU4 and UK, or Japan — and bring a nuanced understanding of how market dynamics differ across regions.
- You work effectively across functions, with a solid understanding of how commercial strategy, market access and pricing, and regional insights teams each contribute to asset success.
- You are comfortable navigating the full medicine lifecycle — from proof-of-concept through in-market management — and understand how insights activities evolve at each stage.
- You communicate complex findings with clarity and confidence, translating analytical outputs into compelling narratives that resonate with senior stakeholders and drive informed decisions.
- English fluent, additional languages are a plus

What we offer: We are curious minds that come from a broad range of backgrounds, perspectives, and life experiences. We believe that this variety drives excellence and innovation, strengthening our ability to lead in science and technology. We are committed to creating access and opportunities for all to develop and grow at your own pace. Join us in building a culture of inclusion and belonging that impacts millions and empowers everyone to work their magic and champion human progress!

Apply now and become a part of a team that is dedicated to Sparking Discovery and Elevating Humanity!

jobs.occupation: Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description:
Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Museum of Natural History in Görlitz, ideally as of April 1, 2027:

Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track)

(full time / part time options available)

Location: Görlitz

Employment scope: full time / part time options are available

Type of contract: initially limited to three years; 

the type of time limitation depends on individual profile and legal framework (maximum 3+3 years). A permanent employment is planned after a positive evaluation

Remuneration: collective agreement of the German Länder, TV-L E13

The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.

The renowned Senckenberg Museum of Natural History, located in the medieval town of Görlitz, combines research at an international level with extensive collections and an engaging museum program. The surrounding Upper Lusatia region offers a large variety of opportunities for experiencing nature.

Senckenberg is committed to study the causes and effects of biodiversity loss in the Anthropocene. As part of our strategic development, we launched an ambitious long-term research effort in “Anthropocene Biodiversity Loss” encompassing the modules “Collectomics”, “Biodiversity Genomics”, and “Solution Labs”. Objectives include the transformation of natural history collections into the digital era, studying biodiversity from the genome to the ecosystem levels and offering exploratory spaces for science and society to develop common solutions to Anthropocene challenges.

For the Görlitz vertebrate collection, which comprises approximately 70,000 specimens (preserved using dry, cryogenic, and liquid preservation methods, with the focus on mammals; birds make up a smaller proportion, while other vertebrate groups represent only a small fraction), we are seeking an internationally recognized scientist with a solid track record in mammal research, possibly supplemented by work on another vertebrate groups.

Potential research topics may include various aspects such as mammalian diversity, functional morphology, phylogeny, or biological interactions. Curation and collection-based research should play a significant role in the applicant’s research approach. The selected candidate should be open to research collaborations with SGN colleagues

Your tasks

- Scientific curation and development of the vertebrate collection and the associated resources as an important international research infrastructure through international networking, growth, and improved accessibility.
- Develop a visible portfolio of collection-based research with basic and applied aspects in the broad field of mammalogy and possibly other vertebrate groups by using a range of established and innovative methods and approaches.
- Taking responsibility for the relocation of the collection items, including the infrastructure of the Mammalogy/Vertebrate Section, to the new campus at Bahnhofstraße 30 at Görlitz.
- Secure external research funds.
- Publish results of your research in international scientific outlets.
- Establish collaborations with ongoing projects, regional and national region (e.g., long-term projects on wolf, lynx) and international (e.g., Africa, Mongolia), including with other sections and departments in Görlitz and further Senckenberg institutes.
- Communicate with external stakeholders such as scientific associations, conservation agencies, local and regional authorities, as well as citizen scientists.
- Participate in teaching in the MSc level programs of International Institute Zittau/ Dresden University of Technology.

Your profile 

- Doctoral degree in biology/zoology or a related field
- Expert knowledge of mammals, including native species (the biogeographic focus of the mammal collection is currently the Palearctic), additional expertise in other vertebrate groups
- Proactive willingness to implement innovative research approaches, such as in the field of genomics, morphometrics, AI, imaging, 3D methods, pollutant analysis in a collection context
- Ability to identify attractive research questions and make use of synergies through collaborations
- Excellent academic track record adequate to your career stage
- Experience in the acquisition of third-party funding and project management
- Experience in supervising staff (doctoral candidates, BSc., MSc., students, technical staff), ability to work in a team
- Very good command of German (B2)
- Fluency in English, both spoken and written
- Class B driving licence (international driving licence)
- Willingness to travel on occasion to the extent possible considering your personal circumstances

Desirable skills 

- Knowledge in molecular, biochemical or biophysical techniques in taxonomy and ecology
- Knowledge in research data management and databases
- Experience in curation and management of zoological collections, and in museum work

We offer 

- Access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations
- An attractive job within the inspiring and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution with excellent infrastructures and collaborations opportunities, e. g. in morphology, genomics, evolutionary biology, (paleo-)ecology
- A working place in completely new building with dissection and other laboratories, collection rooms, in the historic town of Görlitz with rapidly developing local research community (DZA, CASUS, IHI/TUD, HiLusatia), yet situated very close to nature with high mammal diversity and opportunities for field work
- Opportunities to participate in teaching and outreach activities, e.g., in our museum and with collaborating universities
- Opportunities for establishing an independent academic working group and acquiring further academic qualifications
- Flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card  with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement  – company pension plan

Senckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Women are particularly encouraged to apply as they are underrepresented in the field of this position; in the case of equal qualifications and suitability, they will be given preference. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.

How to apply? 

Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV, certificates of academic achievements, list of publications as well as letter(s) of recommendation, if available) as a single PDF file by November 10, 2026

https://www.senckenberg.de/de/stellenanzeigen/.

For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/ (https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/)

For further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung please visit www.senckenberg.de (http://www.senckenberg.de)
